review.brief_reason: The rewrite is not valid under gplearn's protected operators. In particular, log(log(sqrt(q))) cannot generally be replaced by log(log(q)/2), because the protected log threshold is applied before the algebraic identity. The rational regrouping involving powers of q can also alter protected-division behavior. Both expressions remain defined on all real inputs under the stated protected semantics, and variable identities are unchanged.
review.counterexample: Let mom=0, r=0, q=0.0001. Then sqrt(q)=0.01 and protected log(sqrt(q))=ln(0.01), so the original final term is -ln(|ln(0.01)|)≈-1.52718. But protected log(q)=0 because |q|<=0.001, making the proposed final term -log(0/2)=0. At this input the preceding rewritten rational subexpression evaluates to 1 in both forms, so the complete expressions differ.
